# Results — Study 355 (Magnificent-Seven)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The "Mag 7" basket (AAPL, MSFT,
GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, META, TSLA), equal-weight, monthly-rebalanced, raced against the S&P 500
(SPY) and an equal-weight basket of the same mega-cap field. We split the claim in two: is the
outperformance a **stable, forward-tradable factor**, or a **selected, look-ahead concentration
bet** — these seven named *because* they won? Offline & deterministic from the cache; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance monthly **total return** (auto-adjusted closes, public, no key) |
| Window | **2015-08 → 2026-05** (130 complete months) |
| Universe | **40** US mega-caps: the Mag 7 + 33 also-rans (JPM, JNJ, XOM, CSCO, INTC, IBM, DIS, KO, PFE, T, VZ, GE, AMD, …) |
| Benchmark | SPY (S&P 500 total-return proxy) |
| Panel fingerprint | `52a10ec50b92` |

> **Scope caveats (named on the axes).** *Signal* — both the universe **and** the Mag-7
> membership are **current-membership projected back** (look-ahead): the seven are nameable only
> *because* we already know 2015-2026, and the field excludes any mega-cap that died on the way
> (survivorship). The recent spread is real on this tape; its forward repeatability is the open
> question, and the look-ahead is the reason. One 11-year regime (a mega-cap/AI bull).
> *Tradability* — a 2015 investor could not have named these seven; the placebo below shows how
> much of the "edge" is hindsight.

## Half 1 — the recent spread is REAL on the tape

Equal-weight, monthly-rebalanced; CAGR / annualised Sharpe / max drawdown over the 130 months.

| basket | CAGR | Sharpe | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Mag 7 (named)** | **36.2%** | **1.33** | −45.7% |
| S&P 500 (SPY) | 14.4% | 0.96 | −23.9% |
| Equal-weight field (1/N of all 40) | 19.0% | 1.16 | −27.0% |
| Mag 7, net of 10 bps one-way costs | 36.2% | — | — |

HAC (Newey-West) t-stat of the monthly spread:

| spread | mean | HAC t | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Mag 7 − SPY | **+19.9%/yr** | **3.41** | 130 |
| Mag 7 − equal-weight field | +15.8%/yr | 2.88 | 130 |

The spread clears `t ≥ 2` on the real tape — even *after* stripping the "equal-weight beat
cap-weight" effect (the equal-field control), the residual name-selection spread is still
`t = 2.9`. So on the realised tape the seven genuinely out-earned, and it is not just a
weighting trick. **The recent outperformance is real.**

## Half 2 — but it is selection-after-the-fact (the look-ahead placebo)

The Mag-7 *selection rule*, made explicit: with the **full sample in view**, pick the seven
**highest-realised-return** names of the field and hold them. This is pure look-ahead — and it
manufactures an even larger spread:

| selection rule | CAGR spread vs SPY |
|---|--:|
| **Mag 7 (the famous seven)** | **+21.8%/yr** |
| Ex-post "pick the 7 winners" (look-ahead) | **+29.8%/yr** |
| Random *blind* 7-basket (mean / median of 2,000 seeded draws) | +4.1% / +3.1% /yr |

- The hindsight winners are `NVDA, AMD, TSLA, GOOGL, AAPL, MSFT, AMZN` — six of the seven, **plus
  AMD** (the seventh hindsight winner is AMD, not META). The Mag-7 label is ~6/7 of the ex-post
  top-of-the-pile, i.e. it *is* the winners-known-in-hindsight basket.
- The ex-post selection rule alone reproduces **137%** of the Mag-7 CAGR spread — selection is not
  *part* of the edge, it is the whole edge (and then some).
- The Mag 7 sits at the **99.7th percentile** of 2,000 random 7-baskets from the same field. A
  *blindly* chosen seven beat SPY by only ~4%/yr. The other ~21.8% − 4% is the gap between a
  random pick and a hand-picked-with-hindsight one — i.e. selection.

## Synthetic positive control — selection manufactures a spread on a NO-EDGE tape

A deterministic monthly panel (fixed seed) where a *pre-named* basket carries an
``alpha_spread`` and everyone else is identical. The pre-named basket is the honest factor; the
ex-post "pick the winners" rule is the placebo.

| tape | pre-named basket spread (t) | ex-post placebo spread |
|---|--:|--:|
| `alpha = 0.000` (NO true edge) | −2.1%/yr (t = −1.15) | **+10.7%/yr** |
| `alpha = 0.004` (real pre-named edge) | +2.0%/yr (t = +1.20) | +11.2%/yr |

The null row is decisive: with **zero** true cross-sectional edge, a forward-nameable basket has
**no** spread (t ≈ −1, indistinguishable from luck), yet the look-ahead "pick the winners" rule
still conjures **+10.7%/yr** out of pure selection. That +10.7% is the size of the artefact the
Mag-7 label carries by construction. The engine is faithful: it finds a spread *only* where one
is planted (pre-named) and manufactures one *whenever* you select on the outcome (ex-post).

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** The Mag-7 minus-SPY spread is real on the realised tape (+19.9%/yr,
  HAC **t = 3.41**, n = 130; t = 2.9 even vs the equal-weight field). But the basket is
  **selected after the fact**: the synthetic null shows selection alone manufactures a large
  spread with *no* true edge, the ex-post "pick the winners" rule reproduces 137% of the Mag-7
  spread, and the seven sit at the 99.7th percentile of random baskets. Real recent spread,
  **look-ahead / survivorship selected** — a `WEAK` going-forward case dressed in a strong
  in-sample t. Hence `MIXED`.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Costs are trivial (a 7-name monthly basket; net CAGR is unchanged to
  the decimal). The mirage is not friction — it is that **you could not have named these seven in
  2015**. The forward-tradable object is a *blindly* chosen seven (~+4%/yr, swamped by a −45%
  drawdown) or a pre-specified factor (which the null shows can be zero). The 21.8%/yr is a
  number only hindsight can buy.
- **A repeatable strategy? — BUSTED.** "Hold the seven that already won" is not a strategy; it is
  a label applied to the realised top of the distribution. Repeat it *forward* — pick seven names
  today and hold a decade — and you get the random-basket distribution (median +3%/yr, a wide
  tail), not +22%. The Mag 7 is yesterday's winners, not tomorrow's.

> **One-line.** The Mag-7 outperformance is genuinely on the tape — and it is the tape that
> *named* the basket: strip the hindsight and a forward-pickable seven beats the index by ~4%,
> not ~22%; the rest is selection.
